text: On a catch-up call, I told my friend Nick Wignall how someone had trained an AI model to write blog posts in my style. It was a pure research exercise on their part. The idea was to train the tool on my past work, then give it the headlines and opening paragraphs of my 2025 posts. Could it generate the rest of each piece in a similar fashion? So I only compared a handful of posts from their AI versions, so it looks fine. The A was fine enough at first glance, but pay attention just a little longer at something from the RFID country. It sounded pretty confident where I would have been doubtful and vice versa and so on. The creator wanted to know if such a model, once it worked properly, of course, could be useful to me. I told him even if it worked perfectly, it wouldn't lie because I don't write a daily blog to crank out a post every day. If that was the point, I'd have switched to AI long ago already. I write a daily blog to make sure I remember how to think it's a daily practice for my brain, a creator. And if not, that's fine too, attract new readers. That's fine too. Nick said, my story reminded him of an interview with writer and Vox, founder Ezra Klein. Klein explained that so far AI hasn't been all that useful to him. He uses it for light research or to structure some data, but that's about it. Why? Because the writer doing the research is what makes the writing unique. When you're using AI as a writer, you're outsourcing the part of the work like Tend Jovian need to do the most. Klein believes. This is why reading actual books in full might now be more valuable than it ever has been. Only if you've seen every word will you discover insights and links in AI would never include in its average driven summary. Nick pointed out the same applies to a writer struggling when creating a piece, when you're stuck and sit there thinking, trying to come up with what's next. That's the valuable part of writing, of attempting to use AI to remove that stuckness. But it's basically cheating and leads to a basic unblaggian. But is it the idea that needs to slot into this gap or just a bad piece of filler that I'll make for a fragile mental bridge? Most readers won't dare to cross the more I think about the happier I am that AI is transforming the world of writing in a way. I think it'll make it even easier to stand out because the more people take shortcuts, the less quality will remain for readers to flock to, even if the overall quantity of options is much larger. The real artists, fighters, makers, they stick with the truth as old as time itself. The suck is why we're here. And only those who overcome it themselves will reap all the rewards of their hard labor.
